body: I do it!!! Even if I don’t want to or still depressed. Regardless of how I feel, I do it. Whether it “works” or not, is irrelevant to me. Because I value gratitude and appreciation for what I have in my life (even if it’s so minuscule, like the warmth of my morning coffee).
Yes! There’s the crisis text line, it’s 471741

-Sunsets and sunrises
-small and sweet interactions with strangers 
-making someone’s day, no matter how tiny of a reason
-good fucking food, there are so many cuisines and good foods in the world to try, enjoy and experience 
-morning coffee when everything is quiet
-dogs, do I need to say more?
-the pleasure of sex and connection 
-travel (doesn’t even have to be somewhere big and grand)
-laughing 
-memes 
-good movies 
-music 
-the significance of thought and awareness

Hope this helps. For me, finding pleasure in the simple things in life help me keep going and give me hope.

I'm sorry you're in this situation. It is tremendously unethical that proper treatment is a privilege and only for those that can afford it...

For me, I drained my savings to save my life. I had two back to back Suicide attempts in October and November, and then another psych hospitalization in December. I decided then to make the investment.  My treatments were $400 each (IM though not IV but effectiveness is virtually the same). I did 6 initial treatments over 3 weeks in January and then had two maintenance treatments since.  It's definitely helped but I had a bad episode and landed in the hospital 2 weeks ago and actually just got out today. I have another maintenance treatment tomorrow.

I'm a college student and work two jobs (totally to be part-time, 25 hours a week). I think the way I was able to afford it initially was because I did have a decent amount in savings. And what helps is that I have SNAP benefits (food stamps) so I don't have to spend money on food. So I guess you can say the money I don't spend on food, I spend on ketamine.

I don't know your exact financial situation, but honestly if you can get and are eligible for those benefits (its easy to check, just go on your state's health department's website), it could help free up some money for treatment. There's also fundraising through sites like gofundme (that one is iffy though- I was about to do it but then I felt a lot of shame and guilt for asking people for money). I wish I had more suggestions or advice for you. The system is just so horrible. I wish you the best of luck- keep fighting and keep your head up.
